source_name: US Treasury OFAC Press Release sm0099
note: OFAC designated Korea Computer Center (KCC), the state-run IT R&D center (HQ Pyongyang), developer of Red Star OS; reported overseas offices in Germany/China/Syria/India/Middle East; primary official evidence of a Pyongyang IT facility.

source_name: 38 North (Stimson) - Twenty Years of Mobile Communications in North Korea
note: Koryolink 3G launched Dec 2008 with Pyongyang coverage first (Orascom 75%/KPTC 25%); Sunnet 2G by Loxley Pacific 2002 in Pyongyang; Mirae Wi-Fi network (>=33 Mbps) set up in Pyongyang 2017; 1000+ cell base stations mapped via satellite, densest around Pyongyang.
Mirae wireless intranet service works well around Pyongyang (in-country source); SIM registration at service centers/post offices; R&D handled by IT department of Bureau 95, State Affairs Commission.

source_name: Korea IT Times - Korea Computer Center, the Core of North Korea
note: KCC situated in Mangyongdae District, Pyongyang; operates Naenara Information Center (Kwangmyong intranet operator) and a quality management center.

source_name: CSIS - North Korea's Cyber Operations: Strategy and Responses (Cha)
note: KCC located in Sunlae-Dong, Mangyong District, Pyongyang (est. Oct 1990); Pyongyang Informatics Center (PIC) listed among state IT institutions; KCC supports DPRK IT contract workers abroad.
KCC founded 24 Oct 1990 as North Korean government IT research center (HQ Pyongyang); aggregate/secondary source.
Kwangmyong national intranet opened early 2000s, domestic sites on .kp TLD; intranet operated through Naenara Information Center; no public datacenter facility specifications.
North Korean websites offline Jan 2024 amid campaign to overhaul digital infrastructure; evidence of centralised, Pyongyang-hosted web presence.
Samtaesong 8 (三台星/삼태성) smartphone, Android 11, shown on Korean Central TV; evidence of Pyongyang IT hardware ecosystem, NOT a datacenter facility.

source_name: Sand Times (Korean) - Kang Song vs Koryolink subscribers
note: Kang Song network ~3.0M vs Koryolink ~1.7M subscribers (2025); three mobile operators (Koryolink/Kangsong/Byol); subscriber metrics for Pyongyang-centric mobile networks.
Wiki claims Koryolink serves nationwide WCDMA, mainly Pyongyang and inland areas; full 3G data only for approved officials/foreigners; unverifiable wiki source.

source_name: K2Base (NIA, Korea) - .kp domain approval / Kwangmyong expansion
note: Korean government research portal: Kwangmyong fiber network expanded Pyongyang-wide 2004, to Hamhung/Chongjin 2005; intranet under Ministry of Information Industry; useful KO-language source.

source_name: North Korea Tech (Martyn Williams) - Kwangmyong tag
note: Long-running OSINT coverage of Kwangmyong intranet upgrades (search/translation functions); key open-source tracker of NK digital infrastructure.

source_name: CSIS - Responding to the DPRK IT Worker Threat
note: DPRK IT workers estimated to generate $350-800M annually (2024); Pyongyang-based institutions coordinate IT labor export; indirect evidence of centralised IT sector.

source_name: Japan MOFA - Release of the 2nd Report of the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT)
note: Official release of MSMT 2nd report on DPRK cyber and IT worker activities; sanctions-monitoring evidence of the state IT apparatus.

source_name: 38 North - Assessing the MSMT's DPRK IT Worker Threat Report
note: Analysis of MSMT report: DPRK IT workers earn roughly $3,500-$10,000/month; scale of state-run remote IT operations.
Mirae wireless intranet works well in Pyongsong (provincial capital); only IT-infrastructure evidence found for the province; no commercial datacenter known.
Mirae Wi-Fi extended beyond Pyongyang to at least Pyongsong and Nampho; 38 North Digital Atlas shows cellular base-station coverage across the province.
Sinuiju: new surveillance cameras near the Yalu River, '5G technology' claim from a single in-country source; only tech-related item found for North Pyongan; NO datacenter evidence.
No open-source evidence of datacenter/IT facilities in Chagang (capital Kanggye); EN+KO searches returned nothing; province is industrial/military with no public ICT records; treat as no projects.
Mirae wireless intranet works well in Nampo (port city); telecom node on the west coast; no commercial datacenter evidence.
Mirae Wi-Fi extended to Nampho; cellular coverage mapped around Nampo in the 38 North Digital Atlas.
Sunnet 2G cellular network switched on Nov 2002 in Rason AND Pyongyang by Loxley Pacific (Thailand) - first mobile network deployment in Rason; suspended May 2004.

source_name: YouTube field video - Network search in Rason (KANGSONG NET)
note: Field video showing Kang Song network available in Rason; unverifiable video source.
Open-source geospatial dataset incl. telecom infrastructure; recommended for satellite-based enumeration of base stations/infrastructure in the Rason SEZ and nationwide.
